planets.name: Moon
planets.tagline: Lunar South Pole & Mare Basalt Exploration

missions.name: Permanent Habitat
missions.description: Find locations suitable for long-duration base operations, radiation shielding, thermal stability, and living conditions.

missions.name: Rover Operations
missions.description: Identify sites for testing and operating robotic rovers, Lunar Terrain Vehicles (LTV), and autonomous navigation.

missions.name: Scientific Research
missions.description: Find environments for astrobiology, biosignature preservation, mineralogy, and geological field studies.

missions.name: Surface Operations
missions.description: Locate areas for testing EVA suits, ISRU drills, dust mitigation, and surface equipment deployment.

targetRegions.name: Shackleton Crater Rim
targetRegions.description: Artemis candidate region featuring near-continuous solar illumination on the rim adjacent to Permanently Shadowed Regions (PSRs) containing potential water ice.
targetRegions.sourceName: NASA LRO/LOLA & Artemis III Science Definition Report

targetRegions.name: Malapert Massif
targetRegions.description: Elevated peak near the Lunar South Pole offering direct Earth line-of-sight communications and high solar illumination for permanent base infrastructure.
targetRegions.sourceName: NASA Moon Image Galleries / LRO LOLA

targetRegions.name: Mons Mouton Plateau
targetRegions.description: Flat-topped mountain adjacent to Nobile Crater selected for NASA VIPER and Artemis candidate landing studies due to gentle rover-friendly slopes.

targetRegions.name: Nobile Rim 1
targetRegions.description: Artemis candidate region bordering Nobile Crater, offering access to cold-trap volatiles and ancient South Pole-Aitken basin ejecta.

targetRegions.name: Mare Tranquillitatis
targetRegions.description: Equatorial basaltic mare plain hosting Apollo 11 landing site and deep volcanic pit/lava tube skylights that offer natural radiation shielding.
targetRegions.sourceName: NASA ACD-50044 Lunar Surface Data Book

targetRegions.name: Jezero Crater
targetRegions.description: 45 km impact crater and NASA Perseverance rover landing site featuring ancient river-delta sediments, magnesium carbonates, and phyllosilicates.
targetRegions.sourceName: NASA NTRS — Mars 2020 Perseverance Jezero Campaign

targetRegions.name: Gale Crater
targetRegions.description: 154 km impact crater explored by NASA Curiosity rover; records transitions from ancient lakes to hyperarid sulfate-bearing dunes with 0.67 mSv/day surface radiation.

targetRegions.name: Mawrth Vallis
targetRegions.description: One of the thickest phyllosilicate clay-mineral exposures on Mars, closely paralleled by intrabasaltic bole beds in Earth's Deccan Traps.
targetRegions.sourceName: NASA Mars Trek & Planetary Analog Literature

targetRegions.name: Arcadia Planitia
targetRegions.description: Low-elevation smooth volcanic plain with shallow buried water-ice glaciers, prioritized in NASA human landing site studies for ISRU water access.
targetRegions.sourceName: NASA Mars Fact Sheet & Human Landing Site Studies

targetRegions.name: Valles Marineris
targetRegions.terrainType: Tectonic Canyon System (4,000 km × 7 km deep)
targetRegions.description: Largest canyon system in the Solar System (4,000 km long, up to 7 km deep), exposing deep crustal stratigraphy and extreme slope gradients.
targetRegions.sourceName: NASA Mars Fact Sheet & ESA Mars Express

earthSites.name: Atacama Desert
earthSites.description: Earth's driest non-polar desert, featuring high UV radiation, perchlorate-rich soils, and salars used extensively by NASA to test Mars rovers and life-detection instruments.
earthSites.whyAnalogTemplate: Shares hyperarid desiccation, perchlorate/evaporite soil chemistry, high UV flux, and exposed volcanic-sedimentary terrain ideal for Mars rover and biosignature testing.
earthSites.nasaReference: NASA JPL & Astrobiology — Mars Rover & Biosignature Analog

earthSites.name: Haughton Impact Crater
earthSites.description: 23 km impact crater in the Canadian High Arctic hosting the NASA Haughton-Mars Project (HMP) for Moon and Mars EVA, rover, and habitat operations.
earthSites.whyAnalogTemplate: Offers impact-crater morphology, polar permafrost, and extreme operational isolation used by NASA to simulate both Lunar South Pole and Martian crater missions.
earthSites.nasaReference: NASA JPL — Haughton-Mars Project Terrestrial Analog

earthSites.name: Death Valley National Park
earthSites.geologyType: Alluvial Fans, Basaltic Craters (Ubehebe) & Salt Flats
earthSites.description: Used by NASA Mars 2020 and Ingenuity/drone teams to test autonomous navigation, radar altimetry, and rover mobility across dunes and alluvial fans.
earthSites.whyAnalogTemplate: Provides Mars-like aeolian dunes, alluvial fan deltas, and evaporitic basins validated by NASA for rover and aerial drone testing.
earthSites.nasaReference: NASA Planetary Analog Explorer — Death Valley

earthSites.name: McMurdo Dry Valleys
earthSites.description: Ice-free Antarctic valleys where extreme cold, katabatic winds, and permafrost mimic Martian mid/high-latitude subsurface ice and Lunar polar cold traps.
earthSites.whyAnalogTemplate: Matches sub-zero thermal regimes, ice-cemented permafrost, and extreme isolation critical for Lunar South Pole and Martian polar base analogs.
earthSites.nasaReference: NASA Astrobiology — Antarctic Dry Valleys Analog

earthSites.name: Mauna Kea Volcanic Tephra
earthSites.description: High-altitude volcanic summit used by NASA RESOLVE and Pacific International Space Center for Exploration Systems (PISCES) for lunar ISRU and regolith excavation.
earthSites.whyAnalogTemplate: Contains basaltic tephra similar to lunar mare regolith, useful for lunar ISRU, oxygen-extraction, and rover-traction studies.
earthSites.nasaReference: NASA NTRS — Mauna Kea Analog Field Test

earthSites.name: Holuhraun & Askja Volcanic Field
earthSites.description: Used for Apollo astronaut lunar-geology training and as a field analog for Artemis geological navigation across dark basaltic lava flows.
earthSites.whyAnalogTemplate: Replicates fresh basaltic lava morphology, rootless cones, and rugged terrain for lunar rover and EVA geology training.
earthSites.nasaReference: NASA Astrobiology & Planetary Analog Studies — Iceland

earthSites.name: Río Tinto
earthSites.description: Iron- and sulfate-rich acidic river system matching Martian jarosite and hematite deposits discovered in Meridiani Planum and Gale Crater.
earthSites.whyAnalogTemplate: Mirrors Martian iron-oxide and sulfate mineralogy (jarosite/hematite) formed during ancient aqueous alteration.
earthSites.nasaReference: NASA NTRS — Río Tinto Mars Geochemical Analog

earthSites.name: Lonar Crater Lake
earthSites.geologyType: Deccan Flood Basalt Impact Breccia & Alkaline Lake
earthSites.description: 1.2 km meteorite impact crater in basaltic Deccan terrain, making it a close terrestrial analog for impact craters in the Moon's basaltic maria. Its alkaline lake also has limited relevance to studies of ancient Martian paleolakes.
earthSites.whyAnalogTemplate: Combines impact-crater morphology with basaltic bedrock, providing a terrestrial analog for craters in the Moon's basaltic maria.
earthSites.nasaReference: Frontiers in Astronomy & Space Sciences (Jangir & Dutta 2026) / NASA ADS

earthSites.name: Ladakh Cryosphere & Puga Valley
earthSites.geologyType: Ophiolites, Silica Sinters, Permafrost & Alkaline Lakes
earthSites.description: High-altitude (>4 km) cold desert combining freeze-thaw permafrost, intense UV radiation, and alkaline hot springs analogous to ancient Mars hydrothermal systems and lunar cold traps.
earthSites.whyAnalogTemplate: Combines high UV flux, low atmospheric pressure, permafrost, and silica-sinter hydrothermal deposits analogous to ancient Mars and lunar polar highlands.
earthSites.nasaReference: Frontiers in Astronomy & Space Sciences (Jangir & Dutta 2026)

earthSites.name: Deccan Traps & Bole Beds
earthSites.geologyType: Olivine/Pyroxene Basalts & Fe/Mg Smectite Bole Beds
earthSites.description: One of Earth's largest flood basalt provinces; its intrabasaltic bole beds preserve layered phyllosilicates closely paralleling Martian terrains like Mawrth Vallis.
earthSites.whyAnalogTemplate: Matches Martian mafic basaltic crust and the layered Fe/Mg smectite clay alteration found at Mawrth Vallis.
earthSites.nasaReference: Frontiers in Astronomy & Space Sciences (Jangir & Dutta 2026) / Craig et al. 2017

earthSites.name: Thar Desert
earthSites.environmentType: Arid Sand Dunes & Iron-Oxide Dust Storms
earthSites.geologyType: Silicate Dunes, Evaporite Crusts & ~10% Iron-Oxide Dust
earthSites.description: Arid dune field experiencing mineral dust storms (~10% iron oxides) used to study aeolian transport, dust-storm optical scattering, and rover mobility.
earthSites.whyAnalogTemplate: Simulates Martian aeolian dune fields and iron-oxide mineral dust storms for calibrating rover mobility and optical dust-detection sensors.
earthSites.nasaReference: Frontiers in Astronomy & Space Sciences (Jangir & Dutta 2026)

earthSites.name: Sambhar Hypersaline Lake
earthSites.description: India's largest inland saline-alkaline lake undergoing wet-dry evaporite cycling, serving as a direct analog for Martian evaporitic basins and episodic brines.
earthSites.whyAnalogTemplate: Replicates episodic desiccation, steep salinity/pH gradients (pH 9–10), and carbonate-evaporite biosignature preservation seen in Martian paleolakes.
earthSites.nasaReference: Frontiers in Astronomy & Space Sciences (Jangir & Dutta 2026)

earthSites.name: Ibn Battuta Centre, Morocco
earthSites.geologyType: Devonian Carbonates, Sedimentary Rocks, Quartz Sands & Salts
earthSites.description: Located near Erfoud and Merzouga in southeastern Morocco. The supplied research brief describes dunes, hamada, wadis, dry lakes, Devonian Kess Kess carbonate mounds, and the MARS2013 and 2018 ESA rover field trials. Elevation, slope, and normalized feature ratings are approximate.
earthSites.whyAnalogTemplate: Dry lakes, salts, clays, scattered rocks, dust-devil activity, and rover trials make this a useful Mars field-operations analog. Thermal figures and normalized feature ratings are estimates from the supplied brief, whose climate comparison is approximate.
earthSites.nasaReference: Supplied research brief; MARS2013; ESA rover trials (2018); NASA Mars Fact Sheet; Icarus 456 (2026), 117133

earthSites.name: Gorgona Island
earthSites.description: A 9 km by 2.5 km volcanic island in the Pacific Ocean, reaching a maximum elevation of 338 m. Its terrestrial analogy to Syrtis Major is based on volcanic geology; the island's rainforest climate is not Mars-like. Slope and normalized feature ratings are approximate.
earthSites.whyAnalogTemplate: The supplied research brief estimates approximately 89% geological similarity to Syrtis Major for basalt, komatiite, gabbro, and peridotite. Its high humidity and rainfall are strong environmental differences, so its value is primarily geological; climate and normalized feature ratings are approximate.
earthSites.nasaReference: Supplied research brief; NASA Mars Fact Sheet; Icarus 456 (2026), 117133; Astrobiology 18(10) (2018); Astrobiology 14(5) (2014)

earthSites.name: East Uweinat Plain & Gebel Kamil Crater
earthSites.environmentType: Hyperarid Landing Plain & Fresh Impact Crater
earthSites.geologyType: Quartz Sand, Cretaceous Sandstone, Iron Meteorite Fragments & Impact Glass
earthSites.description: Southwestern Egypt's flat East Uweinat plain surrounds the young Gebel Kamil meteorite crater: about 45 m wide and 10 m deep, with a raised rim and ejecta rays. The supplied brief reports 2009–2010 LiDAR and geophysical surveys. Elevation, slope, and normalized feature ratings are approximate.
earthSites.whyAnalogTemplate: Flat, dry landing terrain next to a fresh crater and ejecta field supports touchdown stability, plume-surface dust, LiDAR, and crater-hazard avoidance trials. Quartz-rich geology differs from lunar basalt and anorthosite; thermal comparisons and normalized feature ratings are approximate.
earthSites.nasaReference: NASA Artemis III; NASA SSERVI; Folco et al. (2010), Science 329(5993), 804–807; Urbini et al. (2012), Meteoritics & Planetary Science 47(11), 1842–1868

earthSites.name: Gebel Qatrani, Fayoum
earthSites.environmentType: Basalt Plateau, Escarpments & Dry Gravel Plains
earthSites.geologyType: Oligocene Flood Basalt, Fe/Ti Oxides, Sandstone & Limestone
earthSites.description: North of Lake Qarun in the Fayoum Depression, Gebel Qatrani has dark Oligocene flood basalts, stepped escarpments, talus slopes, and dry gravel plains. The supplied brief describes basalt-regolith simulant and construction-material research. Elevation, slope, and normalized feature ratings are approximate.
earthSites.whyAnalogTemplate: Basaltic feedstock and rugged escarpments support lunar-mare regolith, habitat anchoring, regolith shielding, sintering, 3D-printing, and oxygen-extraction studies. Thermal comparisons and normalized feature ratings are approximate.
earthSites.nasaReference: NASA Artemis Base Camp; NASA STMD MMPACT; Lotfy & Odling (2010), Journal of African Earth Sciences 58(2), 325–340
